display.title: Episode 233: Saved by Miracle, Chapter 2 (Rosh Chodesh Tammuz)
display.summary_short: On Rosh Chodesh Tammuz, Uncle Yossi tells why Yud-Beis Tammuz is a day of joy. A first-grade class sings about the Rambam, and Reb Boruch learns how the Alter Rebbe's advice saved his life.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Tammuz 5746. Uncle Yossi explains that Tammuz holds both sad and happy days, and focuses on the happy one: Yud-Beis Tammuz, when the Frierdiker Rebbe was freed from Soviet prison in 1927 on his own birthday. He had been jailed for teaching Torah to Jewish children, and his release opened the way for yeshivos around the world, so the day is one of thanks and good resolutions. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from Yeshiva Ohalei Torah leads the Shema, and their rebbe introduces a song the boys sing naming the fourteen books of the Rambam's Mishneh Torah. A sponsor message follows. Story time concludes 'Through the Eyes of a Tzaddik': a week later the Alter Rebbe sends Reb Boruch to the minister, who greets him with joy. Officers had been ordered to shoot him had he come that Tuesday, but witnesses then exposed Alex's plot, and Reb Boruch gets his job back with a raise. The show ends with more Sefer Torah contest entrants and Rosh Chodesh wishes.
display.lesson: Things that look puzzling to us look different through the eyes of a tzaddik; trust Hashem and the advice of the tzaddikim.
